title_en: Wenchang Yinghai Qinglan Water Affairs Co., Ltd. v. Wenchang City Ecology and Environment Bureau of Hainan Province et al. — dispute over administrative penalty and administrative reconsideration
ruling_gist_en: Environmental administrative penalties should implement the principle of proportionality between penalty and fault, taking into account factors such as the cause of the violation, circumstances of the violation, subjective fault, degree of harm, and corrective actions, and impose a penalty commensurate with the nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of the illegal act.

full_text_en:
Wenchang Yinghai Qinglan Water Co., Ltd. v. Hainan Province Wenchang City Ecological Environment Bureau et al. — Administrative Penalty and Administrative Reconsideration Case

[Ruling Gist]

Environmental administrative penalties should adhere to the principle of proportionality, taking into account factors such as the cause of the violation, the circumstances of the violation, subjective fault, the degree of harm, and the status of remediation, to impose a penalty commensurate with the nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of the illegal act.

For the conduct of operating before completing the acceptance inspection without subjective fault and without causing harm, if the project has passed the completion acceptance inspection before the penalty is imposed, the administrative agency should not impose an administrative penalty.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Judgment

(2022) Zui Gao Fa Xing Zai No. 329

Retrial Petitioner (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Wenchang Yinghai Qinglan Water Co., Ltd. Domicile: Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant, Qingqun Village Committee Section, Wencheng Town, Wenchang City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Li Yongzheng, Executive Director of the company.

Agent ad litem: Lin Qiuneng, lawyer at Hainan Changyu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lou Chunyan, lawyer at Hainan Changyu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Hainan Province Wenchang City Ecological Environment Bureau. Domicile: 1st Floor, West Building, Municipal Government Compound, Qinglan Development Zone, Wenchang City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Yun Dashi, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Xie Dongliang, staff member of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Luo Changli, lawyer at Hainan Kaizhi Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Hainan Province Wenchang City People's Government. Domicile: Municipal Government Compound, Qinglan New District, Wencheng Town, Wenchang City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Chong, Mayor of the city.

Agent ad litem: Li Ming, staff member of the Municipal Bureau of Justice.

Agent ad litem: Chen Haitao, lawyer at Hainan Falisin Law Firm.

The Retrial Petitioner, Wenchang Yinghai Qinglan Water Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yinghai Company), dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2020) Qiong Xing Zhong No. 658 rendered by the Hainan High People's Court in the case of administrative penalty and administrative reconsideration against the Respondents, the Wenchang City Ecological Environment Bureau of Hainan Province (hereinafter referred to as the Wenchang Environmental Bureau) and the Wenchang City People's Government of Hainan Province (hereinafter referred to as Wenchang City Government), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the administrative ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Xing Shen No. 6733 on May 20, 2022, granting the retrial and initiating proceedings. After the retrial was initiated, a collegial panel was formed in accordance with the law to hear the case. The trial is now concluded.

The facts found by the courts of first and second instance are as follows: The Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant (hereinafter referred to as the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant), constructed and operated by Yinghai Company, is located in the Qingqun Village Committee section, Wencheng Town, Wenchang City, Hainan Province. Construction commenced in 2012, was completed in 2014, and began operation on January 1, 2017. On March 5, 2012, the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau entered into the "Supplementary Contract for the Franchise (BOT) of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project" (hereinafter referred to as the "BOT Contract") with Yinghai Company. On April 24, 2017, the Wenchang City Government issued Wen Fu Han (2017) No. 350 "Reply on the Franchise Period of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant" (hereinafter referred to as Reply No. 350), approving the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau to execute the BOT Contract, with the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant to conduct a trial operation for three months from January 1, 2017. During the trial operation, if the treated sewage effluent met the specified conditions, after passing the online monitoring acceptance, the company should promptly commission a qualified monitoring unit to conduct environmental protection acceptance monitoring. If the monitoring passed, an application for environmental protection acceptance could be submitted to the Wenchang Environmental Bureau. After the environmental protection acceptance was passed, the plant could apply for formal operation. On November 23, 2017, Haikou Hengke Testing Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haikou Hengke Testing Company) issued a "Statement on the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project" (hereinafter referred to as the "Disagreement Statement") to the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau, stating that the production load of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant had not reached over 75% of the designed capacity, and the Wenchang Environmental Bureau did not agree to conduct the completion environmental protection acceptance for the project.

On July 11, 2018, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau conducted an on-site inspection of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant and found that the supporting environmental protection facilities required for the plant had not passed acceptance inspection but were put into use without authorization. On July 23, 2018, the Hainan Provincial Environmental Monitoring Center Station conducted a monitoring survey of the treatment effect of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant. On August 24, 2018, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau issued a "Report on the Investigation and Monitoring Situation of the Sewage Treatment Effect of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant in Wenchang City" (hereinafter referred to as the "Wenchang Environmental Bureau Report"), concluding that the sewage treatment volume was far below the designed treatment load; the influent concentration was far below the design requirements; the pollutant treatment efficiency had long failed to meet the design requirements; the treated sewage from the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant met the discharge standards. The report recommended that the construction unit should, in accordance with relevant documents, conduct the project acceptance on its own and implement it; accelerate the renovation and construction of the sewage collection pipeline network in the Qinglan area to solve the "two lows" problem.

On August 20, 2018, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau issued Wen Huan Bao Gui Gai Zi (2018) No. 38 "Decision on Ordering Correction of Illegal Acts" (hereinafter referred to as Order No. 38), stating that the on-site inspection revealed that the supporting environmental protection facilities of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant had not passed acceptance inspection and were put into use without authorization, violating the provisions of Article 19 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Environmental Protection." Pursuant to Article 23 of the said Regulations, Yinghai Company was ordered to complete the environmental protection acceptance formalities by November 30, 2018; if the formalities were not completed within the specified time, it would be dealt with according to law and regulations. On November 17, 2018, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau issued Wen Huan Bao Fa Jue Zi (2018) No. 29 "Administrative Penalty Decision," imposing a fine of RMB 300,000 on Yinghai Company. Yinghai Company paid the fine.

On December 20, 2018, Yinghai Company requested the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau to take the lead in preparing the environmental completion acceptance of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant. On January 3, 2019, the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau issued a "Reply on the Environmental Completion Acceptance of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project," agreeing that Yinghai Company could entrust a qualified institution to conduct the environmental completion acceptance in accordance with relevant regulations. On January 14, 2019, Yinghai Company signed a "Consignment Agreement on the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of the Construction Project" with Hainan Zhonghuanneng Testing Technology Co., Ltd., entrusting it to carry out the completion environmental protection acceptance monitoring for the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant project.

On March 29, 2019, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau again inspected the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant and believed that Yinghai Company had still not completed the environmental protection acceptance formalities and continued production and operation. A case was filed on April 10, 2019. On April 12, 2019, after collective discussion, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau determined that the illegal facts of Yinghai Company were clear and intended to impose a fine of RMB 1,222,100 on Yinghai Company. On April 15, 2019, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau issued Wen Huan Gai Zi (2019) No. 16 "Decision on Ordering Correction of Illegal Acts," stating that Yinghai Company had failed to correct the environmental illegal acts within the time limit and had not submitted a report on the situation of failing to correct the environmental illegal acts within the time limit, and ordered Yinghai Company to immediately correct the illegal acts. On the same day, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau issued Wen Huan Fa Gao Zi (2019) No. 76 "Notice of Administrative Penalty (Hearing)," informing Yinghai Company of the proposed fine of RMB 1,222,100 and that Yinghai Company could submit statements, defenses, and requests for a hearing.

On April 14, 2019, the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant passed the completion environmental protection acceptance, which was publicly announced online from April 16, 2019, to May 14, 2019, with no feedback upon expiration. On May 9, 2019, upon Yinghai Company's application, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau held a hearing to hear Yinghai Company's opinions. On May 15, 2019, the relevant materials for the completion environmental protection acceptance of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant were filed in the national construction completion environmental protection acceptance information system. On May 16, 2019, Yinghai Company submitted a "Report on the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance Work of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant" to the Wenchang Environmental Bureau.

On September 23, 2019, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau issued Wen Huan Fa Jue Zi (2019) No. 51 "Administrative Penalty Decision" (hereinafter referred to as Penalty Decision No. 51), determining that the supporting environmental protection facilities required for the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant constructed by Yinghai Company had not passed acceptance inspection and were put into use without authorization. The Wenchang Environmental Bureau had issued Order No. 38, ordering Yinghai Company to complete the environmental protection acceptance formalities by November 30, 2018. Yinghai Company failed to correct the environmental illegal acts within the time limit and did not submit a report on the situation of failing to correct the environmental illegal acts within the time limit to the Wenchang Environmental Bureau. The above conduct violated Article 19 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Environmental Protection," which states: "For construction projects requiring the preparation of environmental impact reports or environmental impact statement forms, the supporting environmental protection facilities must pass acceptance inspection before the project can be put into production or use; without acceptance inspection or failing the acceptance inspection, they shall not be put into production or use." Pursuant to Article 23 of the said Regulations, it was decided to impose a fine of RMB 1,000,000 on Yinghai Company. Dissatisfied, Yinghai Company applied for administrative reconsideration to the Wenchang City Government. On January 6, 2020, the Wenchang City Government issued Wen Fu Fu Jue Zi (2019) No. 44 "Administrative Reconsideration Decision" (hereinafter referred to as Reconsideration Decision No. 44), upholding Penalty Decision No. 51. Yinghai Company then initiated this administrative litigation, requesting the revocation of Penalty Decision No. 51 and Reconsideration Decision No. 44.

The administrative judgment (2020) Qiong 96 Xing Chu No. 41 of the First Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province held that, in accordance with Article 11 of the "Measures for Environmental Administrative Penalties," if the party fails to make corrections as required by the time limit set for correction, and the illegal act continues or is in a continuous state, it may be deemed a new environmental illegal act. Yinghai Company should have completed the environmental protection acceptance by November 30, 2018, and its failure to correct within the time limit already constituted a new illegal act. The fact that it had completed the environmental protection acceptance filing by May 15, 2019, could not preclude the determination of its illegal nature. Yinghai Company's claim that the inability to complete the environmental protection acceptance should be attributed to the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau was a contractual dispute between Yinghai Company and the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau, which could be resolved through other channels. In summary, the first instance judgment rejected Yinghai Company's claims. Dissatisfied, Yinghai Company appealed.

The administrative judgment (2020) Qiong Xing Zhong No. 658 of the Hainan High People's Court held that the administrative penalty decision challenged by the Wenchang Environmental Bureau was supported by clear and sufficient evidence, correctly applied laws and regulations, and followed legal procedures. Reply No. 350 only approved a three-month trial operation period and required the plant to pass the environmental protection acceptance before applying for formal operation. Yinghai Company's argument on appeal that the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau and the Wenchang Environmental Bureau had agreed to allow the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant to continue operating and that no administrative penalty should be imposed could not stand. The cause of the illegal act was not within the scope of review of the legality of administrative acts in administrative litigation, and Yinghai Company's argument that the failure to pass the environmental protection acceptance was attributable to the government could not stand. The subsequent correction of the illegal act by Yinghai Company could not negate the existence of the illegal facts. In summary, the second instance judgment dismissed the appeal, affirming the first instance judgment.

Yinghai Company applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: 1. The Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant constructed and operated by Yinghai Company was a trial operation for sewage treatment and monitoring with government permission for the purpose of passing the environmental protection acceptance. It constituted "operation before trial inspection," not "operation before acceptance inspection," and did not constitute unauthorized use. 2. After being subjected to the first administrative penalty, Yinghai Company immediately commenced the environmental protection acceptance process and did not constitute a failure to correct within the time limit. 3. The reason Yinghai Company failed to complete the environmental protection acceptance on time was due to the "two lows" (low influent volume and low influent concentration), which in turn were caused by the insufficient construction of the government's sewage collection pipeline network. The relevant responsibility should be borne by the relevant government departments. 4. After receiving the first administrative penalty, Yinghai Company reported to the government requesting the shutdown of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant, but the relevant government departments still required the plant to continue trial operation. Moreover, if the plant stopped treating sewage, it would cause more serious pollution, so the plant could not be shut down. The Wenchang Environmental Bureau, knowing that an unauthorized shutdown would cause more serious environmental pollution, still issued the challenged Penalty Decision No. 51, violating the principles of law-based administration, reasonable administration, and proportionality. 5. Before Penalty Decision No. 51 was issued, the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant had already passed the completion environmental protection acceptance, yet the Wenchang Environmental Bureau still imposed the penalty, violating the principle of reasonable administration. In summary, Yinghai Company requested: revocation of the first and second instance judgments; revocation of Penalty Decision No. 51 and Reconsideration Decision No. 44.

The Wenchang Environmental Bureau argued: 1. The trial operation period of Yinghai Company should be based on the three-month period approved by the government. When the trial operation period had expired without extension, the continued operation without environmental protection acceptance constituted unauthorized operation. 2. Yinghai Company should have actively conducted its own acceptance inspection. There was no situation where the Wenchang Environmental Bureau disagreed with Yinghai Company's acceptance inspection. 3. Yinghai Company's claim regarding the "two lows" and the construction of the pipeline network was a dispute over the administrative agreement between Yinghai Company and the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau, which should be resolved separately. The reason for not passing the acceptance inspection was not a factor to be considered in the administrative penalty. 4. The fact that Yinghai Company completed the environmental protection acceptance before the penalty decision could not preclude the illegality of the failure to correct within the time limit. 5. When imposing the penalty, the Wenchang Environmental Bureau had considered the fact that the environmental protection formalities had been completed and adjusted the penalty amount from RMB 1.22 million to the minimum fine of RMB 1 million within the statutory range.

The Wenchang City Government argued: The fact that Yinghai Company operated without authorization without passing the acceptance inspection was clear. The Wenchang Environmental Bureau had imposed the lightest fine within the discretionary range, which complied with the principles of law-based administration and reasonable administration.

The facts found by this Court are consistent with the basic facts found by the original trial courts.

This Court holds that this case arose from the Wenchang Environmental Bureau's determination that Yinghai Company's operation of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant after the expiration of the trial operation period, without completing the completion acceptance inspection of the relevant environmental protection facilities as required, constituted "operation before acceptance inspection" and thus imposed a penalty. The original trial judgments have already found that the sewage treated and discharged by the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant met the national standards and reached the discharge standards. The peculiarity of this case lies in: after the expiration of the three-month trial operation period approved by the Wenchang City Government, due to the lag in the construction of the sewage collection pipeline network, the volume and concentration of sewage transported to the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant were low, and the plant's operating conditions could not reach 75% of the designed capacity. The Wenchang Environmental Bureau, in accordance with regulations, disagreed with the environmental protection acceptance inspection. At the same time, the Wenchang City Government and the Wenchang City Water Affairs Bureau, due to the actual need for sewage treatment, disagreed with suspending operation. Under these circumstances, the issue is whether the environmental protection department's re-imposition of a penalty for violating the provision that "without acceptance inspection or failing the acceptance inspection, the project shall not be put into production or use" is lawful and commensurate with the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of Yinghai Company's illegal act. Specifically, this case involves four focal points: (1) the purpose of the completion environmental protection acceptance inspection system and the change of the acceptance inspection entity; (2) the reason for Yinghai Company's failure to obtain the environmental protection acceptance inspection and the change of the acceptance inspection standards; (3) subjective fault and voluntary correction of Yinghai Company's "operation before acceptance inspection"; and (4) the lawfulness and necessity of the challenged penalty decision.

(1) On the purpose of the completion environmental protection acceptance inspection system and the change of the acceptance inspection entity

The "three simultaneous" system is an important management system established by China's environmental protection laws. Among them, the completion environmental protection acceptance inspection system for construction projects serves as a safeguard measure to monitor the implementation of environmental impact assessment document requirements, and is a significant component of the "three simultaneous" system. With the transformation of government functions and the advancement of the reform of the administrative approval system, combined with the practical needs of environmental protection, relevant legislation has continuously reformed and improved the completion acceptance inspection system, with continuous simplification and optimization of the acceptance inspection entity, procedures, and standards. Article 26, paragraph 1 of the 1989 "Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China" stipulated that "The facilities for the prevention and control of pollution in a construction project must be designed, constructed, and put into use simultaneously with the main project. The facilities for the prevention and control of pollution must pass the acceptance inspection by the environmental protection administrative department that originally approved the environmental impact report before the construction project can be put into production or use." Article 20 of the 1998 "Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Environmental Protection" stipulated that "After the completion of a construction project, the construction unit shall apply to the environmental protection administrative department that approved the environmental impact report, environmental impact statement form, or environmental impact registration form for the completion acceptance inspection of the supporting environmental protection facilities." However, the 2014 revision of the "Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China" explicitly deleted the provision in paragraph 1 of Article 26 of the pre-revision law that "The facilities for the prevention and control of pollution must pass the acceptance inspection by the environmental protection administrative department that originally approved the environmental impact report before the construction project can be put into production or use." On this basis, the "Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Environmental Protection" revised on July 16, 2017, abolished the administrative licensing for completion environmental protection acceptance inspection of construction projects, reformed the acceptance inspection entity and supervision method, and changed the entity responsible for completion acceptance inspection from the environmental protection department to the construction unit, and changed the ex-ante acceptance inspection permission of the environmental protection department to in-process and ex-post supervision. Article 17 of the said Regulations stipulates: "After the completion of a construction project that requires the preparation of an environmental impact report or an environmental impact statement form, the construction unit shall, in accordance with the standards and procedures prescribed by the environmental protection administrative department of the State Council, conduct the acceptance inspection of the supporting environmental protection facilities and prepare an acceptance report. During the acceptance inspection of the environmental protection facilities, the construction unit shall truthfully inspect, monitor, and record the construction and commissioning of the environmental protection facilities of the construction project, and shall not engage in fraud. Unless otherwise required by the state for confidentiality, the construction unit shall publicly disclose the acceptance report to the society in accordance with the law."

In this case, the Wenchang Municipal Government issued Reply No. 350 on April 24, 2017, requiring Yinghai Company to apply to the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection for environmental protection acceptance after monitoring passed during the trial operation period. Haikou Hengke Testing Co., Ltd. issued a "Notice of Disagreement with Acceptance" to the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau on November 23, 2017, stating that the environmental protection department disagreed with the completion acceptance. During the second acceptance in 2019, Yinghai Company organized the acceptance by itself in accordance with the new regulations and passed it. It is evident that the completion acceptance of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant project coincided with the transition period between the old and new completion acceptance systems. However, the revised "Regulations on the Administration of Environmental Protection for Construction Projects" had already come into effect on October 1, 2017. After that date, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection no longer had the administrative authority to organize acceptance. Yinghai Company could organize acceptance by itself and compile a qualified acceptance report truthfully to commence formal operation. Therefore, after the new regulations came into effect, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection should have taken the initiative to provide administrative guidance and promptly inform Yinghai Company to organize acceptance as soon as possible. Instead, it informed the testing unit that it disagreed with the completion acceptance. This not only violated the provisions and reform direction of the new regulations but also objectively created a situation where the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant was faced with the dilemma of "operating without acceptance" after the expiration of the trial operation period.

(2) Regarding the reasons for the failure of Yinghai Company's environmental protection facilities to pass completion acceptance and the change in acceptance standards

Haikou Hengke Testing Co., Ltd.'s "Notice of Disagreement with Acceptance" has already stated: "The designed scale of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant is 20,000 m3/d, while the actual scale is 5,000 m3/d. The production load has not reached more than 75% of the designed capacity. The Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Ecological and Environmental Protection disagrees with the project's completion environmental protection acceptance."

Article 9.1.1 of the "Technical Requirements for the Inspection and Acceptance of Environmental Protection Facilities for Construction Projects (Trial)" issued in 2000 stipulates: "For industrial production-type construction projects, acceptance monitoring should be conducted under stable working conditions and when the production load reaches more than 75% of the designed production capacity (if national or local emission standards have other provisions on production load, those standards shall prevail)." Therefore, using the standard of reaching a production load of more than 75% (hereinafter referred to as the 75% acceptance working condition standard) as the technical standard for the completion acceptance of environmental protection facilities has corresponding provisions as its basis. However, whether the production load of an enterprise reaches the 75% acceptance working condition standard depends on multiple factors. The completion acceptance of environmental protection facilities for construction projects should focus on whether the working conditions of the construction project are stable, whether the environmental protection facilities can operate normally, and whether the actual working conditions are truthfully recorded and monitored. It should not be rigidly bound to the 75% acceptance working condition standard. Reaching a production load of more than 75% is always a gradual process. Requiring all sewage treatment plants that have not reached the 75% acceptance working condition standard to not pass acceptance, and thus not be allowed to be put into use, can easily trap construction projects in a dilemma: operation constitutes a violation and faces penalties; cessation of operation makes it impossible to gradually improve working conditions, thus never reaching the 75% acceptance working condition standard, and never being able to obtain completion acceptance. This situation not only prevents the sewage treatment plant from being effectively utilized but also runs counter to the original intent of the "Three Simultaneities" system and the completion acceptance system for environmental protection facilities. "The law should not demand the impossible." At least for some construction projects, the 75% acceptance working condition standard should be revised. The "Decision on Abolishing Certain Regulations and Normative Documents of the Environmental Protection Department" issued by the Ministry of Environmental Protection on July 13, 2016, explicitly abolished the 75% acceptance working condition standard. Article 5, paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 of the "Interim Measures for the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of Construction Projects," effective in November 2017, stipulate: "After the completion of a construction project, the construction unit shall truthfully inspect, monitor, and record the construction and commissioning of the environmental protection facilities of the construction project, and prepare an acceptance monitoring (investigation) report. For construction projects that mainly discharge pollutants, the acceptance monitoring report shall be prepared by reference to the 'Technical Guide for Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of Construction Projects - Pollution Impact Category'." Article 6.1 of the "Technical Guide for Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of Construction Projects - Pollution Impact Category" released in May 2018 further stipulates: "Acceptance monitoring should be carried out under the condition that the main project's working conditions are stable and the environmental protection facilities are operating normally, and the actual working conditions at the time of monitoring, as well as the key parameters that determine or affect the working conditions, should be truthfully recorded. The main indicators that can reflect the operating status of environmental protection facilities should be truthfully recorded. Recommended methods for recording working conditions during the acceptance monitoring period for typical industries in main projects, environmental projects, and auxiliary projects are detailed in Appendix 3." The new technical specifications removed the requirement that the working conditions during acceptance monitoring should reach more than 75%, and clarified that acceptance monitoring should be carried out under the condition that the main project's working conditions are stable and the environmental protection facilities are operating normally, with truthful recording of the actual working conditions at the time of monitoring.

In this case, after the "Decision on Abolishing Certain Regulations and Normative Documents of the Environmental Protection Department" came into effect on July 13, 2016, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection should no longer have applied the 75% acceptance working condition standard. Furthermore, after the revised "Regulations on the Administration of Environmental Protection for Construction Projects" came into effect on October 1, 2017, it should have taken the initiative to provide administrative guidance to the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant, urging it to entrust completion acceptance as soon as possible in accordance with the new regulations, without further consideration of the 75% acceptance working condition standard. However, the "Notice of Disagreement with Acceptance" fully proves that the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection continued to implement the 75% acceptance working condition standard at least between April and November 2017, and continued to exercise the completion acceptance authority, objectively causing the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant to fail to obtain timely completion acceptance and create the dilemma of "operating without acceptance." The corresponding adverse consequences should not be borne entirely by the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant.

(3) Regarding Yinghai Company's subjective fault and active rectification of "operating without acceptance"

According to Article 49, paragraph 3 of the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution," the competent construction department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the construction plan for urban sewage treatment facilities, organize the construction of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities and supporting pipeline networks, and strengthen the supervision and management of the operation of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities. According to Article 8.3 of the "BOT Contract" signed between the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau (Party A) and Yinghai Company (Party B), Party A shall ensure that throughout the entire concession period, sewage is collected and conveyed to the delivery point of the sewage treatment project, basically meeting the water quantity and influent water quality requirements stipulated in Article 9 of this contract. Therefore, the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau is not only responsible for constructing supporting pipeline networks and collecting sewage but also for ensuring that the collected sewage meets the basic water quantity and influent water quality requirements. The "Report of the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection" submitted by the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection to the Wenchang Municipal Government on August 24, 2018, also stated that the daily influent volume was 51% of the designed daily treatment capacity, and the sewage treatment volume was far from reaching the designed treatment water load; the influent pollutant concentration was less than 50% of the designed influent water quality concentration, with the concentration of main pollutants in the influent being severely low. The report recommended accelerating the renovation and construction of the sewage collection pipeline network and implementing new pipeline network construction to address the "two lows" problem of low influent water volume and low influent pollutant concentration. It can be seen that the production load of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant not reaching 75% of the designed capacity was caused by the "two lows" resulting from inadequate construction of the supporting pipeline network for sewage collection, for which Yinghai Company had no subjective fault.

To resolve the "two lows" problem as quickly as possible and pass the completion environmental protection acceptance, after receiving the first administrative penalty, Yinghai Company actively communicated with the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau and proactively submitted a report to the Wenchang Municipal Government. The "Minutes of the Special Meeting on Studying the Problems of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project" issued by the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau on April 23, 2018, stated that the meeting studied issues such as the completion acceptance of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant project, required resolving the "two lows" problem of the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant as soon as possible, and that the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau should complete the construction of the Qinglan area sewage interception and confluence project (Phase II) as soon as possible to collect sewage from the area east of Gaolong Avenue and Baijin Road; and accelerate the preliminary work of the Qinglan area sewage interception and confluence project (Phase III) to strive for early commencement and construction. The "Report of the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection" submitted by the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection to the Wenchang Municipal Government on August 24, 2018, also recommended accelerating the renovation and construction of the sewage collection pipeline network in the Qinglan area to solve the "two lows" problem.

To accelerate the completion acceptance, Yinghai Company also submitted an "Application for the Completion Environmental Acceptance of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project" to the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau on December 20, 2018, earnestly requesting the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau to support and take the lead in carrying out the completion environmental acceptance of the project. On January 3, 2019, the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau issued a "Reply on the Completion Environmental Acceptance of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project" to Yinghai Company, agreeing that Yinghai Company could entrust a qualified agency to carry out the completion environmental acceptance of the project in accordance with regulations. On January 14, 2019, Yinghai Company signed an "Agreement on Entrusting Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of Construction Projects" with Hainan Zhonghuanneng Testing Technology Co., Ltd., entrusting it to carry out completion environmental protection acceptance monitoring. On April 14, 2019, the acceptance working group issued the "Opinions on the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant Project," finding that the project basically met the conditions for national construction project completion environmental protection acceptance and agreeing to pass the completion environmental protection acceptance. The relevant information was also made public online, and the project's completion environmental protection acceptance materials were filed on the National Construction Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance Information System on May 15, 2019. On May 16, 2019, Yinghai Company submitted a "Report on the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance Work of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant" to the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection, reporting on the completion of the completion environmental protection acceptance work. On May 23, 2019, Yinghai Company submitted a "Report on the Application for Formal Operation of the Wenchang Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant" to the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau, applying for formal operation.

The above shows that the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection was aware of the reasons why the production load had not reached the 75% acceptance working condition standard for a long time, namely that the "two lows" of influent volume and influent concentration were mainly due to the government's insufficient construction of the supporting pipeline network for sewage collection. These were neither controllable by Yinghai Company nor its responsibility, and it had no subjective fault. One month after the first penalty decision was made, Yinghai Company requested the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau to take the lead in carrying out the completion environmental acceptance work, entrusted a testing company to carry out the completion environmental acceptance, and completed all acceptance procedures four months before the second penalty decision was made. It had the subjective intention to rectify the illegal state and objectively took the initiative to correct the illegal act according to the guidance of the administrative agency. Yinghai Company had no subjective fault for failing to eliminate the state of "operating without acceptance" in a timely manner and actively made corrections. When imposing administrative penalties, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection should have conducted a comprehensive, objective, and fair investigation and collected evidence unfavorable and favorable to the party. It should have also considered factors such as the objective cause of the illegal act, subjective fault, and other circumstances. Its claim that the objective cause of the illegal act should not be considered does not comply with the provisions of Article 36 of the "Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the "Administrative Penalty Law") as amended in 2017, which requires "must conduct a comprehensive, objective, and fair investigation and collect relevant evidence." The view of the original trial judgment that the cause of the illegal act does not fall within the scope of legality review of administrative acts in administrative litigation is legally incorrect and should be corrected.

(4) Regarding the legality and necessity of the penalized penalty decision

Article 4, paragraph 2 of the "Administrative Penalty Law" stipulates that the establishment and imposition of administrative penalties must be based on facts and commensurate with the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of the illegal act. Article 27, paragraph 2 stipulates that if the illegal act is minor and corrected promptly, without causing harmful consequences, no administrative penalty shall be imposed. Article 6, paragraph 1 of the "Measures for Environmental Administrative Penalties" stipulates that the exercise of discretionary power in administrative penalties must conform to the legislative purpose and comprehensively consider the following circumstances: the degree of environmental pollution and ecological damage caused by the illegal act and its social impact; the degree of fault of the party; the attitude of the party in correcting the illegal act and the corrective measures taken and their effects, etc.

The Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant constructed and operated by Yinghai Company has a public welfare nature of purifying and treating sewage, preventing water pollution, protecting water ecology, protecting and improving the environment, and maintaining public health. This is different from enterprises that generate and discharge sewage. The "Report of the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection" issued by the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection also determined that the sewage treated by the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant met the discharge standards, and all pollutant indicators complied with the limits of the "Discharge Standard of Pollutants for Municipal Wastewater Treatment Plants (GB18918-2002)." Therefore, although Yinghai Company had the situation of "operating without acceptance," it not only did not cause any consequences of environmental pollution or ecological damage but was instead beneficial to environmental protection.

Yinghai Company claimed that after receiving the first administrative penalty, it submitted a report to the Wenchang Municipal Government requesting the temporary shutdown of the sewage treatment plant but received no response. The Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau also notified Yinghai Company by letter on November 16, 2018, agreeing to accept sewage discharged from 16 local catering units, and on December 12, 2018, notified Yinghai Company by letter, requesting it to connect the sewage discharged by Hainan Qinfu Food Co., Ltd. to the plant for treatment. Moreover, shutting down the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant, which meets all discharge indicators, could cause a large amount of local production and domestic sewage to go untreated and be directly discharged into the sea, causing environmental pollution. There is also a risk of secondary pollution from pollutants such as wastewater, waste liquid, and waste residue retained in the sewage treatment plant. The "Opinions on Further Deepening Ecological and Environmental Supervision Services to Promote High-Quality Economic Development" (Huan Zonghe [2019] No. 74) issued by the Ministry of Ecological and Environmental Protection on September 8, 2019, stipulates that it is strictly prohibited to take simple and crude measures such as emergency shutdowns, suspensions, or stoppages indiscriminately to cope with inspections, as well as perfunctory practices such as "shut down all" or "stop first, talk later." The rectification of related ecological and environmental problems should be conducted in accordance with laws and regulations, with a focus on comprehensive promotion and the establishment of long-term mechanisms. The reason why the Qinglan Sewage Treatment Plant was "operating without acceptance" was based on the requirements of relevant departments and the objective needs of sewage treatment. It acted in good faith without subjective fault. Although it formally violated legal provisions, it was consistent with legal principles and legislative intent and would not cause consequences of environmental pollution.

According to Article 4, paragraph 13 of the "Guiding Opinions on Further Standardizing the Application of Discretionary Power in Environmental Administrative Penalties" (Huan Zhifa [2019] No. 42) issued by the Ministry of Ecological and Environmental Protection, if an illegal act such as "starting construction without approval" does not cause environmental pollution consequences, and the enterprise voluntarily implements shutdown or takes measures such as stopping construction or production, the penalty may be exempted. Other minor illegal acts that are promptly corrected and cause no harmful consequences may also be exempted from penalties. When investigating and handling the case, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection should have referred to the spirit of this article and comprehensively considered the cause and consequences of the illegal act of "operating without acceptance." However, it failed to do so, and the exercise of its discretion was improper. Even if the first penalty of RMB 300,000 imposed by the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection for "operating without acceptance" had some degree of legality and necessity, after Yinghai Company accepted the administrative penalty, it promptly, in accordance with the provisions of the "Interim Measures for the Completion Environmental Protection Acceptance of Construction Projects," actively communicated with government departments to promote the construction of supporting pipeline networks, proactively requested the Wenchang Municipal Water Affairs Bureau to take the lead in carrying out the completion environmental acceptance work, and completed the completion acceptance before the second penalty decision was made. Under these circumstances, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection's imposition of a fine of RMB 1,000,000 on an enterprise with an annual total sewage treatment fee income of only RMB 3 to 5 million was neither lawful, nor reasonable, nor necessary, and could easily give rise to suspicion of shirking responsibility for higher-level environmental protection inspections.

In summary, "the law should not demand the impossible." Although Yinghai Company objectively committed the illegal act of "operating without acceptance," it had no subjective fault. The re-imposition of a penalty on it was not only inconsistent with the principle of good faith and civilized law enforcement but also incompatible with the rule of law requirements for the construction of the Hainan Free Trade Port. When making the penalized penalty decision, the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Environmental Protection failed to fully consider the particularity of the "operating without acceptance" illegal act of the sewage treatment plant, and failed to fully consider factors such as the objective cause of the illegal act, harmful consequences, subjective fault, and subsequent corrective measures. The exercise of discretion was clearly improper, and the decision should be revoked. The No. 44 review decision, which wrongly upheld the administrative penalty decision that should have been revoked, should also be revoked. The first and second instance judgments dismissing Yinghai Company's claims applied the law incorrectly and should be reversed by law. In summary, pursuant to Article 70 and Article 89, paragraph 1, item 2 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," and Article 119, paragraph 1 and Article 122 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke Administrative Judgment No. (2020) Qiong 96 Xing Chu 41 of the First Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province and Administrative Judgment No. (2020) Qiong Xing Zhong 658 of the Hainan High People's Court;

2. Revoke the No. (2019) 44 Administrative Review Decision of the People's Government of Wenchang City, Hainan Province;

3. Revoke the No. (2019) 51 Administrative Penalty Decision of the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Ecological and Environmental Protection, Hainan Province.

The court acceptance fees of RMB 100 for the first and second instances shall be borne by the Wenchang Municipal Bureau of Ecological and Environmental Protection, Hainan Province, and the People's Government of Wenchang City, Hainan Province.

This judgment is final.
